title: Late Breaking Results: On-the-Fly Hadamard Hypervector Processing for Efficient Hyperdimensional Computing
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires expensive pre-generation or iterative O(N) search to find orthogonal hypervectors, creating bottleneck for hardware deployment; fixed precomputed vectors limit adaptability.
motivation: HDC's efficiency in high-dimensional processing is offset by vector generation costs; hardware-efficient, on-the-fly generation can unlock practical HDC acceleration with dynamic adaptability.
method: Introduces on-the-fly hypervector generation in hardware using Hadamard binary coefficients with O(1) complexity versus O(N) conventional search. Leverages unary computing and in-memory computing (IMC) to simplify encoding into addition-only operations after generation. ASIC implementation leverages Hadamard properties for efficient hardware realization.
key_novelty: First O(1) on-the-fly Hadamard hypervector generation in hardware, replacing O(N) iterative search with direct generation via binary coefficients.
contributions: O(1) hardware hypervector generation vs O(N) software search
Hadamard binary coefficient-based generation leveraging unary computing
Significant accuracy and computational efficiency improvements across benchmarks
limitations: Evaluation on specific benchmarks; scalability to larger hypervector dimensions and real-world HDC applications not detailed.
primary_theme: O(1) Hadamard-based hypervector generation for HDC acceleration
